notes: fmt: Rust's format!/print!/write!/Display/Debug achieve Printf and Stringer for formats known at compile time (mapped to std). The `printf` module keeps Go's verb engine only for runtime Go-format strings and the differential suite, over an explicit operand model. Go's reflection over `any` operands becomes the Value enum (Arg alias) with From impls for Rust primitives, strings, Vec/array/slice, Option/Box (pointers) and HashMap/BTreeMap; named Go types with methods are Value::Named carrying Display (Go's Stringer), Debug (Go's GoStringer), Formatter and error implementations. Printing is byte exact: every verb, flag, width, precision, `*` and [n] argument index, and the %!verb(type=value), EXTRA, MISSING, BADINDEX, BADWIDTH, BADPREC, NOVERB and PANIC error forms; digits and quoting come from strconv. Panicking String/Error/Format methods are caught with catch_unwind (the default panic hook still reports to stderr). Sprint* return String (invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD; append* are byte exact; Fprint*/Print* are std::write!/print!); Errorf returns fmt::WrapError (std::error::Error; source() is the first %w operand, sources() is Go's Unwrap() []error). Scan* write into ScanArg destinations (typed &mut, `*[]byte` as Vec<u8>, custom Scanner); Fscan* take std::io::Read (one rune of lookahead is lost, as in Go) or, as fscan_runes/fscanln_runes/fscanf_runes, an io::RuneScanner. Not expressible: scanning into pointers to renamed (named) Go types via reflect (use the underlying type's destination), reflect.Value operands, and Printf of arbitrary Go values (build them as Value); %p and %v of pointers print the address carried by the Value. A Rust i32 operand is a Go int32 (use isize or Value::int for Go int) and char is a Go rune (int32).

Errorf.note: Returns a Rust String: invalid UTF-8 in operands becomes U+FFFD; the append forms are byte exact.

Fprint.note: Go adds spaces between non-string operands; printf::append gives those bytes

Fprintf.note: write!(w, ...) for formats known at compile time; printf::appendf for a runtime Go format

GoStringer.note: a value's Debug output is its %#v text (Value::with_debug)

Print.note: Go adds spaces between non-string operands; printf::append gives those bytes

Printf.note: print!(...) for formats known at compile time; printf::appendf for a runtime Go format

ScanState.Read.note: ScanState: std::io::Read; like Go's, its read always fails (use read_rune)

Sprint.note: Returns a Rust String: invalid UTF-8 in operands becomes U+FFFD; the append forms are byte exact.

Sprintf.note: Returns a Rust String: invalid UTF-8 in operands becomes U+FFFD; the append forms are byte exact.

Sprintln.note: Returns a Rust String: invalid UTF-8 in operands becomes U+FFFD; the append forms are byte exact.

Stringer.note: a value's Display output is its %v/%s text (Value::with_display)
